title: Directive: discover what we don't know yet
body: Discover relations that are not yet part of established knowledge. Build on the laws you were given and on your own verified results; prefer bridges between different fields; check every candidate for dimensional consistency and against measurements; never present an untested candidate as established fact.

title: Bayes' theorem
body: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B): the rule for updating belief with evidence.

title: Fourier transform
body: Any reasonable signal is a superposition of sinusoids: F(ω) = ∫ f(t) e^{−iωt} dt.

title: Noether's theorem
body: Every differentiable symmetry of the action yields a conserved quantity (time → energy, space → momentum, rotation → angular momentum).

title: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
body: Any consistent formal system rich enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove.

title: Prime number theorem
body: The number of primes below x is asymptotic to x/ln x.

title: Divergence theorem
body: ∮ F·dA = ∫ ∇·F dV.

title: Newton's first law
body: A body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net force.

title: Newton's third law
body: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

title: Conservation of energy
body: The total energy of an isolated system is constant.

title: Conservation of momentum
body: The total momentum of an isolated system is constant.

title: Conservation of charge
body: Electric charge is neither created nor destroyed.

title: Second law of thermodynamics
body: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

title: Third law of thermodynamics
body: The entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as T → 0 K.

title: Zeroth law of thermodynamics
body: Two systems each in thermal equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other.

title: Principle of least action
body: Physical trajectories make the action S = ∫ L dt stationary; Euler–Lagrange: d/dt(∂L/∂q̇) = ∂L/∂q.

title: Maxwell's equations
body: ∇·E = ρ/ε₀, ∇·B = 0, ∇×E = −∂B/∂t, ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t.

title: Schrödinger equation
body: iħ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ; the wavefunction's evolution is unitary and linear.

title: Born rule
body: The probability density of a measurement outcome is |ψ|².

title: Pauli exclusion principle
body: No two identical fermions occupy the same quantum state.

title: Einstein field equations
body: G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν: matter-energy curves spacetime.

title: Principle of relativity
body: The laws of physics are identical in all inertial frames; c is the same for all observers.

title: Equivalence principle
body: Gravitational and inertial mass are identical; free fall is locally indistinguishable from inertial motion.

title: Standard Model
body: Matter is quarks and leptons; forces are carried by gauge bosons of SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1); mass arises via the Higgs mechanism.

title: Four fundamental interactions
body: Gravity, electromagnetism, weak and strong nuclear forces.

title: Periodic law
body: Element properties recur periodically with atomic number, reflecting electron shell structure.

title: Conservation of mass in reactions
body: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, in chemical reactions.

title: Le Chatelier's principle
body: A system at equilibrium shifts to counteract an imposed change.

title: Aufbau principle and Hund's rule
body: Electrons fill lowest-energy orbitals first and occupy degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins first.

title: Chemical bonding
body: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonds arise from electrostatics and quantum sharing of electrons; VSEPR predicts molecular geometry.

title: Hess's law
body: Reaction enthalpy is path-independent: sum the enthalpies of component steps.

title: Avogadro's law
body: Equal volumes of gases at equal T and P contain equal numbers of molecules.

title: Cell theory
body: All living things are made of cells; cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

title: Evolution by natural selection
body: Heritable variation plus differential reproductive success produces adaptation and common descent.

title: Central dogma of molecular biology
body: Information flows DNA → RNA → protein (with reverse transcription as an exception).

title: Genetic code
body: Triplet codons of nucleotides map to 20 amino acids; the code is nearly universal.

title: Mendelian inheritance
body: Genes come in alleles that segregate and (when unlinked) assort independently.

title: Homeostasis
body: Organisms regulate internal variables via negative feedback.

title: Energy flow in ecosystems
body: Energy flows one way from producers through trophic levels with ~10% transfer efficiency; matter cycles.

title: Germ theory of disease
body: Many diseases are caused by microorganisms.

title: Chemiosmosis
body: ATP synthesis is driven by proton gradients across membranes.

title: Plate tectonics
body: The lithosphere is divided into plates moving over the asthenosphere, driving earthquakes, volcanism and mountain building.

title: Uniformitarianism
body: The same physical processes operating today shaped Earth in the past.

title: Law of superposition
body: In undisturbed strata, younger layers lie above older ones.

title: Greenhouse effect
body: Atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, warming the surface.

title: Rock cycle
body: Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks transform into one another.

title: Big Bang cosmology
body: The universe expanded from a hot dense state ~13.8 billion years ago; evidence: CMB, Hubble expansion, light-element abundances.

title: Stellar nucleosynthesis
body: Stars fuse hydrogen into helium and heavier elements; the heaviest form in supernovae and neutron-star mergers.

title: Kepler's first law
body: Planets move on ellipses with the Sun at one focus.

title: Kepler's second law
body: A line from Sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (conservation of angular momentum).

title: Shannon source coding theorem
body: Data can be compressed to its entropy H = −Σ p log₂ p bits per symbol but no further.

title: Church–Turing thesis
body: Any effectively computable function is computable by a Turing machine.

title: Scientific method
body: Observe, hypothesise, predict, test by experiment, revise; claims must be falsifiable and reproducible.

title: Dimensional homogeneity
body: Every valid physical equation has identical dimensions on both sides; functions like exp, log, sin take dimensionless arguments.

title: Huygens' principle
body: Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; their envelope is the new wavefront.

title: Fermat's principle
body: Light travels between two points along the path of stationary optical length.

title: Pascal's principle
body: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished throughout it.

title: Lenz's law
body: An induced current flows so as to oppose the change in flux that produced it.

title: Superposition principle
body: For linear systems the net response to several stimuli is the sum of the individual responses.

title: Correspondence principle
body: Quantum mechanics reproduces classical physics in the limit of large quantum numbers.

title: Complementarity
body: Wave and particle descriptions are complementary; which appears depends on the measurement.

title: Spin-statistics theorem
body: Integer-spin particles are bosons; half-integer-spin particles are fermions.

title: CPT symmetry
body: Every Lorentz-invariant local quantum field theory is invariant under combined charge conjugation, parity and time reversal.

title: Gauge invariance
body: The fundamental interactions arise from requiring local symmetry of the quantum fields.

title: Bell's theorem
body: No local hidden-variable theory reproduces all predictions of quantum mechanics; experiments confirm the violation of Bell inequalities.

title: No-cloning theorem
body: An unknown quantum state cannot be copied perfectly.

title: Cosmological principle
body: On large scales the universe is homogeneous and isotropic.

title: Holographic principle (conjecture)
body: The information content of a region of space may be bounded by its boundary area in Planck units.

title: Gravitational waves
body: Accelerating masses emit ripples in spacetime travelling at c; first detected directly by LIGO in 2015.

title: Quantum entanglement
body: Composite quantum systems can have joint states not expressible as products of individual states.

title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
body: A system's ground state can lack the symmetry of its laws, producing phases, massless modes, or masses via the Higgs mechanism.

title: Renormalization group
body: Physical theories change systematically with the scale of observation; universality explains why diverse systems share critical exponents.

title: Octet rule
body: Main-group atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to attain eight valence electrons.

title: VSEPR theory
body: Electron pairs around a central atom arrange to minimise repulsion, fixing molecular geometry.

title: Hammond's postulate
body: A transition state resembles the stable species nearest to it in energy.

title: Hückel's rule
body: Planar cyclic conjugated systems with 4n+2 π electrons are aromatic.

title: Markovnikov's rule
body: In HX addition to an alkene, H attaches to the carbon with more hydrogens.

title: Brønsted-Lowry acids and bases
body: Acids donate protons; bases accept them.

title: Lewis acids and bases
body: Acids accept electron pairs; bases donate them.

title: Collision theory
body: Reactions occur when molecules collide with sufficient energy and correct orientation.

title: Transition state theory
body: Reaction rates are set by a quasi-equilibrium with an activated complex at the saddle point of the energy surface.

title: Electronegativity
body: Atoms differ in their pull on bonding electrons; differences determine bond polarity.

title: Born-Haber cycle
body: Lattice energies follow from Hess's law applied to ionisation, electron affinity, sublimation and dissociation steps.

title: Hardy-Weinberg principle
body: Allele and genotype frequencies stay constant without selection, mutation, migration, drift or non-random mating.

title: Hamilton's rule
body: Altruism is favoured by selection when relatedness × benefit > cost (rB > C).

title: Neutral theory of molecular evolution
body: Most molecular variation is selectively neutral and fixed by genetic drift.

title: Endosymbiotic theory
body: Mitochondria and chloroplasts descend from free-living bacteria engulfed by ancestral cells.

title: Competitive exclusion principle
body: Two species competing for the same limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely.

title: Island biogeography
body: Species richness on islands balances immigration (falling with distance) and extinction (falling with area).

title: Red Queen hypothesis
body: Species must continually adapt merely to keep pace with co-evolving competitors and parasites.

title: DNA double helix
body: DNA is two antiparallel strands paired A–T and G–C, enabling templated replication.

title: Action potential
body: Neurons fire all-or-none spikes via voltage-gated Na⁺ and K⁺ channels (Hodgkin–Huxley).

title: Hebbian learning
body: Synapses strengthen when pre- and post-synaptic neurons fire together.

title: Clonal selection
body: Antigens select and expand lymphocytes bearing matching receptors, creating adaptive immunity.

title: Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation
body: Cells oxidise acetyl-CoA to CO₂, and use the resulting electron flow to pump protons and make ATP.

title: Epigenetic inheritance
body: Gene expression states can be inherited through cell division without changes in DNA sequence.

title: Cell cycle and apoptosis
body: Cells divide through regulated checkpoints and can trigger programmed death.

title: Milankovitch cycles
body: Periodic changes in Earth's orbit and tilt pace glacial–interglacial cycles.

title: Carbon cycle
body: Carbon moves among atmosphere, oceans, biosphere and rocks on timescales from years to millions of years.

title: Water cycle
body: Water circulates by evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff, powered by sunlight.

title: Thermohaline circulation
body: Density differences from temperature and salinity drive a global ocean conveyor.

title: Coriolis effect
body: In a rotating frame moving bodies are deflected, shaping winds, currents and cyclones.

title: Wilson cycle
body: Ocean basins open and close cyclically as supercontinents assemble and break apart.

title: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
body: Stars occupy distinct luminosity–temperature regions reflecting mass and evolutionary stage.

title: Cosmic microwave background
body: Relic black-body radiation at 2.7255 K from recombination ~380,000 years after the Big Bang.

title: Cosmic inflation
body: A brief early epoch of exponential expansion explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the seed fluctuations.

title: Dark matter evidence
body: Galaxy rotation curves, lensing, cluster dynamics and the CMB require ~5× more non-luminous than baryonic matter.

title: Accelerating expansion
body: Supernova distances show cosmic expansion is accelerating, attributed to dark energy.

title: Exoplanets
body: Thousands of planets orbit other stars, detected by transits, radial velocities, imaging and microlensing.

title: Central limit theorem
body: Sums of many independent finite-variance variables tend to a normal distribution.

title: Law of large numbers
body: Sample averages converge to the expected value as sample size grows.

title: Fundamental theorem of algebra
body: Every non-constant polynomial has a complex root.

title: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
body: Every integer > 1 factors uniquely into primes.

title: Cantor's diagonal argument
body: The real numbers are uncountable: no list can contain them all.

title: Halting problem
body: No algorithm decides for every program whether it halts.

title: Brouwer fixed-point theorem
body: Every continuous map of a closed ball to itself has a fixed point.

title: Nash equilibrium existence
body: Every finite game has an equilibrium in mixed strategies.

title: Kolmogorov axioms
body: Probability is a non-negative, normalised, countably additive measure.

title: Pigeonhole principle
body: Placing n+1 objects in n boxes puts two objects in one box.

title: Landauer's principle
body: Erasing one bit of information dissipates at least k_B T ln 2 of heat.

title: Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem
body: A band-limited signal is fully reconstructed from samples taken at more than twice its highest frequency.

title: Shannon's channel coding theorem
body: Reliable communication is possible at any rate below channel capacity, and impossible above it.

title: From data: Hydrogen Balmer emission lines
body: Best form found in the data: 1/lam = A + B·1/n^2, with A = 2.74195e+06, B = -1.09676e+07 (rms error 0.0002%). Integer structure: 1/lam = 1.096765e+07·(1/3.9999 − 1/n²); 1/3.9999 ≈ 1/2² — every line ends on level 2. Fitted constant = 1×Rydberg constant to within 0.0554%. The residual ratio 0.9994456 is explained by the factor 1/(1 + m_e/m_p) (predicted 0.9994557): the nucleus is not infinitely heavy — the electron orbits the centre of mass (reduced-mass correction).
status: spectral series law found in data; constant identified

title: From data: Air pressure versus altitude
body: Best form found in the data: log(P) = A + B·h, with A = 11.6046, B = -0.000149263 (rms error 4.7319%). This is exponential decay: P = 1.096e+05·exp(−h/6699.6) — a characteristic scale of 6700 (SI units of height). Connecting to known laws (barometric formula + atmospheric scale height H = RT/(Mg)): the fitted scale height implies a mean air temperature of 228.9 K (-44.3 °C) over this altitude range.
